findings: CONFIRMED: exactly 45 run_record.json files exist, one per (arm in {1,2,5}) x (fold 0-4) x (seed 42-44), no gaps.
CONFIRMED: exactly 45 valid eval/*/metrics.json exist for that same grid, all with plausible non-degenerate values; no error/traceback/failed strings in any of the 45 training logs.

NOT FULLY SUPPORTED AS STATED -- three integrity gaps found: (1) outputs/branch_c/eval/ contains 46 directories, not 45: eval/arm5_f0_s42 is a byte-for-byte-metrics duplicate of eval/arm5_mstcn_556_fr_f0_s42 (differs only in the recorded checkpoint path, relative vs absolute; timestamped ~4 minutes earlier), i.e. a superseded prior invocation left in place. A naive glob of eval/* over-counts by one. (2) outputs/branch_c/RUNS.jsonl (the protocol-§9-mandated append-only provenance ledger) contains only 41 of the 45 'train'-stage entries. The 4 missing entries are exactly arm1_mstcn_553_ff_f0_s42, f0_s43, f0_s44, and f1_s42 -- and those same 4 runs are exactly the 4 (of 45) whose run_record.json['git']['commit'] is bf649f5eb6... instead of ea2a8ad2... (the commit used by all other 41 runs, including every arm2 and arm5 run). So 4/15 of arm1's runs were both trained under different tracked code AND never logged to the provenance ledger. The tracked diff between the two commits touches only fold-manifest data files and orchestration scripts (tools/branch_c/aggregate_arms.py, launch_arm_sweep.py), not model/training code, so this is very unlikely to be a substantive confound -- but run_record.json does not carry a dirty-diff hash (RUNS.jsonl entries do, for the cache stage), so the uncommitted state of those 4 runs cannot be fully audited. (3) A separate, registered arm -- arm0_mstcn_quality, the protocol §5.1 mandatory shortcut audit -- was dispatched for all 5 folds x 3 seeds (outputs/branch_c/arm0_sweep.log: '15 runs to dispatch') but only fold 0's 3 seeds produced any artifact, and those three stop mid-training with no run_record.json and no metrics.json. This is not part of the 45 arm1/2/5 runs and does not affect the 'per_run' claim, but it means the mandatory shortcut audit is incomplete, which the ablations report must not paper over.

go_gate_verdict.reasoning: Protocol §7.1's scientific gate requires arms 6-13 (fusion superstructure) and full-model-vs-arm2 outer-fold evidence that do not exist: arms 6 and 13 were dropped by the pre-registered amendment-A1 gate (FINDINGS §12.15) before training, and arms 3, 4/7-12, 14-17 were never reached. The gate that WAS run and IS independently reproduced here is amendment A1's proxy for §7.1 condition 1: does the validated, 100%-coverage, full-range pose measurement (arm 5) beat the strongest properly-comparable baseline it was meant to upgrade (arm 2)? Recomputed directly from the 45 raw eval/*/metrics.json files: mean paired macro-F1 diff arm5-arm2 = -0.0023, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0123, +0.0084] (20000 draws, seed 0, over the 15 matched fold/seed pairs), 5/15 wins, raw p=0.643, Holm-corrected p=1.000. Required: >= +0.02 absolute with CI excluding zero. Observed: negative, CI straddles zero, off by roughly an order of magnitude. Directional consistency (gate condition 4) also fails: pooling predictions across the 5 folds within each seed before scoring (a stricter, protocol-3.1-style estimator with far less fold-noise) still gives arm5 < arm2 in 2 of 3 seeds. No calibration or fusion conditions (gate conditions 3, 5) are assessable because no fusion arm was trained.
go_gate_verdict.scope_caveat: This verdict covers only the pose-measurement question the branch actually tested. It is not a verdict on the full registered scientific gate, most of whose preconditions (a trained full model) never existed to be tested.
